answer_2.quote: The quality of the generated audio samples is evaluated using three objective metrics: Fréchet Distance (FD), Fréchet Audio Distance (FAD), and Kullback-Leibler divergence (KL). We evaluate each model's controllability using ... nine metrics ... Tempo Bin (TB), Tempo Bin with Tolerance (TBT), Correct Key (CK), Correct Key with Duplicates (CKD), Perfect Chord Match (PCM), Exact Chord Match (ECM), Chord Match in any Order (CMO), Chord Match in any Order major/minor Type (CMOT), Beat Match (BM).
automatic_metrics: Chord Match in any Order major/minor Type (CMOT)

answer_4.quote: We conducted two rounds of subjective evaluation... A total of 48 participants participated in the first round of the general listening test... The participants were asked to rate the: i) audio rendering quality (AQ), ii) relevance of the audio with the input text prompt (REL), iii) overall musical quality (OMQ), iv) rhythm consistency (RC), and v) harmony and consonance of music (HC). For the expert listening test, we added two additional music control-specific aspects ... MCM and MTM (musical chord/tempo match).
answer_4.guideline: Participants rated each generated sample on a 7-point Likert scale for multiple criteria including audio quality, relevance, overall musical quality, rhythm consistency, harmony/consonance, and for experts also chord match and tempo match.
